scope: Unified introduction, market, creator studio, inspection reports, product, checkout and acquired-bot library

design.intro_handoff: Native View Transition API with a shared glass object when visible; fade fallback; reduced-motion branch

browser_checks: The introduction opened automatically on the fresh test browser origin.
The market CTA closed the intro, cleared transition styles, selected the market and focused its H1.
Footer replay followed by the creator CTA opened the studio and focused its H1 on a 320-pixel viewport.
Reload after the intro handoff left the introduction closed.
Name and version inputs updated the studio preview through textContent.
Switching Python to rules and back retained the drafted Python source.
A preview-only source file was loaded during the earlier desktop check; no creator version was submitted in this UI pass.
Searching Signal returned exactly one card; the rules filter returned Proof Trend.
BTC/USD and ETH/USD market labels remained distinct; synthetic product data displayed as a synthetic example.
The Signal Check report displayed -0.98% return, 1.54% drawdown, five fills and all eight inspection checks from its existing public evidence.
Proof Trend checkout displayed 0.01 test NEAR license price plus 0.02 storage allowance, total 0.03, with gas explicitly separate.
The mobile checkout dialog fitted within the viewport and retained license-scope and unused-deposit disclosures.
Mobile product sections appeared in this order: measured performance, additional warnings, purchase, version proof, common benchmark.
A local MIT Atlas example was acquired through the explicitly labeled virtual purchase flow, with no chain transaction.
The acquired example appeared in the library with report, download and retest controls.
The library retest completed all 73 decisions and opened a report with seven inspection checks and three baseline rows.
The acquired example's product screen showed My license instead of another buy action.
Final 320-pixel market had equal document client and scroll widths, both 305 pixels with a 15-pixel scrollbar.
390-pixel market, studio, report, product and library layouts were inspected without document horizontal overflow after corrections.
The temporary viewport override was reset to the normal 1920 x 945 desktop viewport.
The final page reported no console errors; extension-only warnings were not application errors.
The market was left open as the deliverable while the local server remained running.

includes: Exact 24-decimal purchase totals and storage allowance
Owned-product action and actual report risk labels
Source metadata escaping and correct market/synthetic labels
Run, report, hash verification, local entitlement and exact artifact delivery
Cross-origin, owner isolation, forged payment and testnet-payment bypass rejection
automated_checks.environment_note: The sandbox-only HTTP attempt was blocked by loopback EACCES. All 11 checks passed after local-network access was permitted.

limits: This UI pass did not repeat personal-wallet signatures, testnet payments, contract deployment or paid LLM calls. Earlier chain verification remains documented separately.

The current browser automation did not return a download-completion event for the local ZIP. Browser policy also blocked inspection of chrome://downloads. No new saved-file download is claimed; ZIP entitlement/delivery was checked by the HTTP suite, and earlier personal-wallet download evidence remains separate.
Native reduced-motion behavior and the non-View-Transition fallback were reviewed in code without changing OS preferences or forcing browser API removal.
First-visit caching is per browser storage, not cross-device person identification.
